Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. For $i\in I$ and $n\ge1$ the subalgebra $R(n\alpha_i)$ is generated by the polynomial subalgebra $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and the crossings $\tau_1,\dots,\tau_{n-1}$ with $\tau_a^2=0$ (because $Q_{ii}=0$), the braid and far commutation relations, and the nil-Hecke dot moves, i.e. it is the nil Hecke algebra of rank $n$; its PBW basis is $\{x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}\tau_w\}_{a\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n,w\in S_n}$ ([[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]]). Fix a reduced expression $w_0=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_{\binom n2}}$ of the longest element and put $\partial_{w_0}:=\tau_{i_1}\cdots\tau_{i_{\binom n2}}$ (independent of the reduced expression). The **divided-power idempotent** is
$$e_{i,n}:=x_1^{n-1}x_2^{n-2}\cdots x_{n-1}\,\partial_{w_0}\in R(n\alpha_i),$$
and its horizontal reflection is $\psi(e_{i,n}):=\partial_{w_0}x_1^{n-1}\cdots x_{n-1}$. Both are nonzero idempotents of degree $0$, and $e_{i,n}\ne0$ because the PBW basis separates the monomials involved. The **divided-power projective** is
$$P_{i,n}:=R(n\alpha_i)\,\psi(e_{i,n})\{-d_i\tbinom n2\},$$
where the shift is the one fixed by the source normalization: as a graded left module $R(n\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,n})$ is the polynomial representation, it is indecomposable projective, and with this shift $R(n\alpha_i)$ is a finite direct sum of $[n]_i!$ shifted copies of $P_{i,n}$, where $[n]_i!=\prod_{a=1}^n\frac{q_i^{a}-q_i^{-a}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}$ is the $q_i$-factorial of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] (at $q_i=1$ it is $n!$); hence $P_{i,n}$ is the unique indecomposable projective summand up to shift and $\mathrm{End}_{R(n\alpha_i)}(P_{i,n})_0=k$. For a divided-power sequence $\theta=i_1^{(n_1)}\cdots i_r^{(n_r)}$ put $\beta=\sum_an_a\alpha_{i_a}$ and $P_\theta:=\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})$ along the ordered concatenation of the blocks of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]; then $[P_\theta]$ represents the ordered product of these divided powers; one may reorder only by the proved commuting/Serre relations, adjacent colours need not commute, and for a single colour $\theta=i^{(n)}$ one has the indecomposability above.

**Projective duality.** For a finite graded projective left $R(\beta)$-module $P$ put $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$, the $\psi$-twisted graded Hom into the rank-one free module, where $\psi$ is the horizontal-reflection anti-involution. Evaluation $P^\#\to$ (dual of $P$) identifies $(P^\#)^\#\cong P$ for finite shifted free modules, and hence for every finite graded projective; the duality reverses internal shifts and fixes each normalized $P_{i,n}$ after the displayed shift.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and fix a reduced-expression system: for each $w\in S_n$ one reduced word $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_r}$, and for $
u\in I^n$ put $	au_w:=	au_{i_1}\cdots	au_{i_r}\in R_n(Q)$. Then the monomials $	au_wx_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}e(
u)$, over all $w\in S_n$, $a_1,\dots,a_n\ge0$ and $
u\in I^n$, form a $k$-basis of $R_n(Q)$; equivalently $R_n(Q)$ is a free $k$-module on these monomials, and $R( eta)$ has the corresponding basis. Moreover each $R( eta)$ has finite-dimensional homogeneous components, and the graded dimension of the summand $e(
u)R_n(Q)e(
u')$ is the formal Laurent Hilbert series counting the monomials (bounded below, equivalently the finite sum of the corresponding rational geometric series), so the graded ranks are independent of the parameters $Q$: for each fixed $ eta$, $\dim_kR( eta)_m<\infty$ for all $m$ and $R( eta)_m=0$ for $m\ll0$; if $I$ is finite the same holds for $R_n(Q)$. In particular $R( eta)$ is a locally finite graded algebra; its degree-zero part need not be one-dimensional (already $x_1	au_1\in R(2\alpha_i)_0$ is a nontrivial idempotent).

Let $p(u)$ be monic of degree $N\geq0$ over a commutative ring $D$. Let $L_r$ be the monic factor ring $p=c_rb_{N-r}$, where $c_r$ is monic of degree $r$, and put $L_r=0$ for $r<0$ or $r>N$. Put
$$B_r=L_r[z]/b_{N-r}(z)=L_{r+1}[z]/c_{r+1}(z),\qquad h=N-2r.$$
Use the native nil-Hecke crossing $\tau=(1-s)/(X-Y)$ of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], dots of degree $2d$, and the matrix idempotent convention of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]. Induction is $G(r)=B_r\{-2dr\}\otimes_{L_r}-$, basic restriction is the reversed $B_{r-1}$ tensor functor, and normalized restriction at input $r$ is $H(r)=B_{r-1}\{-d(1+h)\}\otimes_{L_r}-$. The first adjunction uses the coefficient form $\tau_{\rm new}:B_r\to L_{r+1}$ extracting $z^r$; the second uses $\tau_{\rm old}:B_r\to L_r$ extracting $z^{N-r-1}$. Units are the trace-dual power-basis Casimirs. Write $\eta:1\to HG$, $\varepsilon:GH\to1$, $\eta':1\to GH$, $\varepsilon':HG\to1$ for these maps, at their indicated input weights.

Set $P=GH$, $V=HG$ at input $r$. Define the actual native mates, rather than freely adjoined inverses, by
$$T=(HG\varepsilon)(H\tau^{GG}H)(\eta GH):P\to V,\qquad S=(GH\varepsilon')(G\tau^{HH}G)(\eta'HG):V\to P,$$
where $\tau^{HH}$ is the twofold first-adjunction mate of $\tau^{GG}$. Put
$$A(t)=t^h\frac{b(t^{-1})}{c(t^{-1})},\qquad \mathsf H(t)=A(t)^{-1},\qquad A_0=\mathsf H_0=1.$$
Coefficients with negative index are zero. For $h\geq0$, let $C_k=x^k\eta$ and
$$R_k=\sum_{a+j=h-1-k}A_j\varepsilon'x^a\quad(0\leq k<h).$$
Then the actual flag bimodule maps $\rho=(-T,C):P\oplus D_h\to V$ and $\sigma=(S,R):V\to P\oplus D_h$ satisfy
$$-ST=1_P,\quad R_kT=0,\quad SC_k=0,\quad R_kC_\ell=\delta_{k\ell},\quad -TS+\sum_kC_kR_k=1_V.$$
For $h<0$, set $C^-_k=x^k\eta'$ and
$$R^-_k=\sum_{a+j=-h-1-k}\mathsf H_j\varepsilon x^a\quad(0\leq k<-h).$$
The maps $\rho=(-T,R^-):P\to V\oplus D_{-h}$ and $\sigma=(S,C^-):V\oplus D_{-h}\to P$ satisfy
$$-TS=1_V,\quad TC^-_k=0,\quad R^-_kS=0,\quad R^-_kC^-_\ell=\delta_{k\ell},\quad -ST+\sum_kC^-_kR^-_k=1_P.$$
Here $D_h=\bigoplus_{k<h}1\{d(1-h+2k)\}$ and $D_{-h}=\bigoplus_{k<-h}1\{d(1+h+2k)\}$. At $h=0$ both sums are empty.

These maps also give the two typed upward curls
$$L_\mu=(H\varepsilon'_\mu)(\tau^{HH}G)(H\eta_\mu),\qquad R_\mu=(\varepsilon_\mu H)(G\tau^{HH})(\eta'_\mu H),$$
where $L_\mu$ has input $\mu$ and $R_\mu$ input $\mu-\alpha_i$, with $\langle h_i,\mu\rangle=h$. Their formulas are
$$L_\mu=\sum_{a+j=-h}x^a\mathsf H_j,\qquad R_\mu=-\sum_{a+j=h}x^aA_j.$$
All indices in these sums are nonnegative. Mating the two matrix-completeness equations gives the two opposite-crossing cancellation equations with literal-dot sum $a+b+c=-2$: the $HG$ boundary uses $A_{b+h+1}$, and the $GH$ boundary uses $\mathsf H_{b-h+1}$. Single curls instead have literal-dot sum $a+b=-1$.

For a symmetrizable datum and distinguished color $i$, take a dominant integral framing $\lambda_i\geq0$ and
$$p(u)=a_i(u)\prod_{j\ne i}\prod_{y\in Y_j}Q_{ij}(u,y)/t_{ij},\qquad t_{ij}=[u^{-a_{ij}}]Q_{ij}(u,y)\in D^\times.$$
This realizes every $r\geq0$, including both signs of $h$, with zero modules past $N$. Appending a color $j$ root uses the quotient and multiplication by $Q_{ij}$, and the mixed mate pair constructed with the first unit/first cap and second unit/second cap has composites $t_{ij}$ in **both** orders. This identifies the actual mixed mates in the distinguished-$i$ flag model. Compatibility with adjunctions for a second distinguished color is a separate assembly question.

Under the nil-Hecke matrix equivalence the first cap is exactly $\tau_{\rm new}$ and the normalized relative second cap is exactly $\tau_{\rm old}$: the normalization is $\widehat\varepsilon_r=(-1)^{N+1}\varepsilon_r$ for the ordered-residue relative form defined in the proof. No formal diagram-model realization, categorical commutator, cyclotomic Frobenius theorem, or one-dimensional Hom hypothesis is a premise. Every assertion is an integral polynomial identity, hence survives arbitrary monic specialization. Grading is asserted only when the coefficients are homogeneous in their natural degrees.

derivations.claim: Monic splitting and the vertex ring. Over universal graded $S=k[p_1,\ldots,p_N]$, successive monic division gives the full splitting Artin basis $X_1^{a_1}\cdots X_N^{a_N}$ with $0\leq a_k\leq N-k$ and perfect coefficient pairing. The two-block staircase and longest-divided-difference retraction of [F4] shows the block-invariant factor ring $L_r$ is finite graded projective over $S$. Lift a homogeneous basis modulo $S_+$; graded Nakayama gives a finite graded free-module surjection onto $L_r$. A projective splitting and the least-degree argument kill its kernel, whose $S_+$ fiber is zero, so $L_r$ is graded free. The full splitting algebra has Artin ranks $N!$ over $S$ and $r!(N-r)!$ over $L_r$, hence the free rank is $\binom Nr$. Base change to the coefficients of $p_m$ proves the claimed finite free $C$-module in every characteristic. For $r>N$ the excessive coefficient ideal contains $1$, since a monic degree-$r$ factor cannot divide degree-$N$ $p_m$, so $L_m=0$.

The vertex ring as a matrix quotient. Representing $\mathrm{NH}_r$ as the matrix algebra on its Artin module (step 1.1, [F2]) shows that the two-sided ideal generated by a monic $p(X_1)$ is the matrix ideal of the coefficients of the remainder of $p$ modulo $c_r$, and monic division makes these coefficients a unit triangular change from the consecutive relations; hence $\mathrm{NH}_r/(p(X_1))$ is the matrix algebra over the monic factor ring $L_m$ of the Statement. The same computation shows the $i$-flag $B_m$ is free of rank $N-r$ over $L_m$ and rank $r+1$ over $L_{m+i}$, giving the two root extensions of the model.

Coefficient maps, triangles and normalized transport. The kernel $K_f(X,Y)=(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$ is the trace-dual power-basis Casimir: coefficient extraction gives $\tau_X(X^aK_f)=Y^a$ in the root quotient. Its contractions prove both adjunction triangles, and symmetry gives cyclic dots. The actual nil-Hecke matrix corners identify induction with $B_m$ and its dual with $g\mapsto[v\mapsto\tau_{\mathrm{new}}(gv)]$ [F4], so evaluation and coevaluation are the stated first cap and cup. The same supplier proves the ordered-residue relative cap normalized by $(-1)^{N+1}=(-1)^{h_m+1}$ transports exactly to $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}$, and its dual unit to that Casimir. This fixes actual second maps, not merely dimensions or trace values. The coefficient forms have degrees $-2d_ir$ and $-2d_i(N-r-1)$; after the basic induction shift their adjunction degrees are $0$ and $-2d_i(h_m-1)$. Normalizing $H_i$ at its input gives first unit/second cap degree $d_i(1-h_m)$ and first cap/second unit degree $d_i(1+h_m)$.

The actual canonical comparison and prescribed inverse. Take the typed native mates $T:G_iH_i\to H_iG_i$ and $S:H_iG_i\to G_iH_i$ built from the actual maps of step 3.1 and the downward crossing and its twofold mate. On equal-endpoint generic root paths their matrices are $(-T)_{z,w}=c(z)/[c'(w)(z-w)]$ and $S_{w,z}=b(w)/[b'(z)(w-z)]$, with $w$ selected and $z$ complementary; swap paths have $T=-1,S=1$ [F4]. Thus they are the two polynomial interpolation maps. At $h_m\geq0$, divide the degree-$<N-r$ interpolant by $c$: its remainder has degree $<r$, and its quotient degree $<h_m$. Expanding $b/c=u^{h_m}A(u^{-1})$ identifies quotient coefficients with the prescribed $R_k=\sum_{a+j=h_m-1-k}A_j\varepsilon'x^a$, with columns $C_k=x^k\eta$. The supplier proves all five equations $-ST=1$, $RT=0$, $SC=0$, $RC=1$, $-TS+CR=1$. At $h_m<0$, division of the degree-$<r$ interpolant by $b$ gives $R^-_k=\sum_{a+j=-h_m-1-k}\mathsf H_j\varepsilon x^a$, $C^-_k=x^k\eta'$ and all five equations $-TS=1$, $TC^-=0$, $R^-S=0$, $R^-C^-=1$, $-ST+C^-R^-=1$. At zero weight both identity blocks are empty. These are identities on actual finite projective tensor bimodules, descended integrally before specialization, with degree-zero components after the prescribed shifts.

Typed curls, cancellation and bubble coefficients. The downward crossing $\kappa=(s-1)/(X-Y)$ has square zero and obeys the braid and mixed dot equations by expansion; the symmetric Casimir gives dot mates. The actual curls of [F4] are $L_\mu=\sum_{a+j=-h_m}x^a\mathsf H_j$ on $H_i$ at input $\mu$, and $R_\mu=-\sum_{a+j=h_m}x^aA_j$ at input $\mu-\alpha_i$, of degrees $-2d_ih_m$ and $2d_ih_m$. Mating the completeness equations of step 4.1 gives the cancellation corrections. Positively, $a+j+c=h_m-1$ and the clockwise bubble has literal dots $b=-h_m-1+j$; negatively, $a+j+c=-h_m-1$ and counterclockwise dots are $b=h_m-1+j$. Both give $a+b+c=-2$, with the prescribed native signs; the single-curl sums give $a+b=-1$. Actual pairings determine the bubble coefficients: $\varepsilon'x^n\eta=\sum_z c(z)z^n/b'(z)$ is the $u^{-1}$ coefficient of $u^nc/b$, namely $\mathsf H_{n-h_m+1}$, whereas $\varepsilon x^n\eta'=\sum_w b(w)w^n/c'(w)=A_{n+h_m+1}$. Here $A(t)=t^{h_m}p_m(t^{-1})/c_r(t^{-1})^2$ and $\mathsf H=A^{-1}$; negative indices vanish and coefficient zero is $1$. Integral descent proves these identities without distinct-root hypotheses after specialization. Thus $\Phi_i=p_m/c_r^2$ has the prescribed normalized series and reciprocal. Appending $i$ root $z$ divides $A$ by $(1-zt)^2$, and appending spectator root $y$ multiplies it by $q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}(y,t)$; reciprocal coefficients give the opposite slides. All recursions are finite at each coefficient. At a monic vacuum, closing $a_i(x)x^{\ell-1}=0$ gives $\mathsf H(t)a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}(t)=1$.

Downward $Q$-relations and exact word grading. Give every flag the ordered shift $s_j(m)$ of the Statement. For $j<k$ the increasing word $(j,k)$ maps to the word $(k,j)$ by a quotient/switch of underlying degree $0$, with target-minus-source unit shift $-b_{jk}$; the reverse operator has underlying degree $-2b_{jk}$ and unit-shift $+b_{jk}$, so both have actual degree $-b_{jk}$, and same-color divided differences have degree $-2d_j$. Native operators are the negatives of the source operators, so their degrees and two-crossing composites are unchanged. The ordinary polynomial operators satisfy the idempotent, dot, far-commutation and quadratic $Q$-relations directly; expanding a three-strand composition gives zero difference for distinct outer colors and the divided difference of $Q$ for equal outer colors, and the global substitution $\kappa=-\tau$ changes all cubic signs to the native numerator. The quotient relations descend: on an $i,j$ pair $D_1$ has $bq=0$ and $D_0$ has $b=0$, and $Qb=t_{ij}bq$ makes multiplication by $Q$ well defined while the other crossing is the literal quotient.

The typed partial-color mixed pair. At input $\mu$ put $\xi=\mu+\alpha_i-\alpha_j$, $X=G_jH_i$, $Y=H_iG_j$. The native maps are $a=(H_iG_j\varepsilon_\mu)(H_i\tau^{G_iG_j}H_i)(\eta_\xi G_jH_i):X\to Y$ and $b=(\varepsilon'_\xi G_jH_i)(H_i\tau^{G_jG_i}H_i)(H_iG_j\eta'_\mu):Y\to X$. Their middle words are $H_iG_iG_jH_i$ and $H_iG_jG_iH_i$; final counits consume respectively the rightmost $G_iH_i$ and leftmost $H_iG_i$. For $p'=pq_{ij}$, [F4] proves the actual normalized cap equation $\pi\widehat\varepsilon^{p'}(Q_{ij}\operatorname{lift}(z))=t_{ij}\widehat\varepsilon^p(z)$ with lift independence on every matrix-corner element, and its dual cup equation. The ordered-residue sign $(-1)^{N+1}$ transports precisely to $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}$ of step 3.1. Substituting the quotient/switch and multiplication-by-$Q$ in the two mate contractions therefore proves $ba=t_{ij}1_X$ and $ab=t_{ij}1_Y$ for this same pair. Source crossings negate both maps and preserve the products. They commute with the $j$ dot and have degree $d_i(1+h_m)+d_i(-1-h_m+a_{ij})-b_{ij}=0$, giving the unshifted mixed isomorphism. The separately distinguished-$j$ model has its own scalar $t_{ji}$; a full two-color adjunction comparison is not a relation of the category containing only $H_i$.

Conclusion. Steps 3.1-7.1 verify every defining relation of [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]] on the explicit flag modules: the generators and their degrees, both adjunction triangles, the rank-one matrices in both branches with their inverses, the bubble series and slides, the cross-and-cap equations, the mixed isomorphism with its scalars, and the downward $Q$-relations. Monic extensions, their Casimirs, the finite rank-one inverses and the coefficient identities survive arbitrary monic specialization as ungraded maps, and the construction is choice-free. This proves only the formal MODEL relations; faithfulness and the cyclotomic word-corner transfer belong to separate suppliers.
